text:
The latest Laravel 13.x releases, including **v13.34.0** from September 29, 2026, introduce significant changes affecting queue workers, focusing on both critical compatibility adjustments and functional enhancements for robustness and management [1][2].

## Key Breaking Change: Queue Serialization Incompatibility

The most critical update for queue workers in Laravel 13 is the adoption of a new, more compact job serialization format. This change renders jobs queued by a Laravel 12 application incompatible with Laravel 13 workers, meaning Laravel 13 workers will fail to process older jobs. Consequently, applications upgrading to Laravel 13 must **fully drain their queues** before deploying Laravel 13 workers to avoid job failures [3]. Additionally, Laravel 13 requires a minimum PHP version of **8.3** (or 8.4 depending on the specific patch version), necessitating a PHP upgrade alongside the framework [4][\_mGaig].

## Enhanced Worker Management and Robustness

Recent 13.x releases (including **v13.34.0**, **v13.33.0**, **v13.30.0**, and **v13.26.0**) bring numerous improvements to queue worker stability and control [5].

**Smarter Timeout Handling**: Queue workers now feature more intelligent timeout handling. Developers can **opt out of worker termination** when a job times out, providing greater control over worker behavior. This enhancement includes dropping `restart_syscalls` from `pcntl_signal` within the worker process [5][6].

**Improved Error and Crash Reporting**: Laravel **v13.34.0** introduced the capability for jobs to count unexpected worker crashes towards their `maxExceptions` limit. This offers clearer insights into job failures that stem from worker instability rather than job logic, preventing endless retries [5][7]. Furthermore, the `queue:restart` command now provides more effective error messages when a worker cannot be restarted, aiding in faster debugging [8][5].

**Increased Visibility and Control**: Workers can now surface paused queues in their output, and the `queue:work` command explicitly outputs the reason a worker stopped. For more granular control over queue management, a new `--queue` option has been added to the `queue:flush` command [5].

**Event Object Refinements**: Queue-related events have been refined for better information flow. The `JobAttempted` event now directly exposes the **exception object** (`$event->exception`) that caused the job attempt to fail, replacing the less informative boolean `$event->exceptionOccurred`. For consistency across queue events, the `$connection` property in the `QueueBusy` event has been renamed to `$connectionName` [4][9].

## Conclusion

These comprehensive changes collectively aim to make Laravel's queue system more robust, transparent, and manageable for developers. While the new serialization format presents a critical upgrade consideration requiring careful queue draining, the enhancements to worker management, error reporting, and event handling ultimately lead to a more reliable and observable queue infrastructure.

sources.title: Laravel 13 (2026) Release: New Features and Upgrade Guide - PHP Everyday
claims: Laravel 13 introduces typed configuration retrieval, throwing a ConfigTypeMismatchException if a value does not match the declared type.
The query builder in Laravel 13 uses prepared statement caching by default, showing 15-25% improvement on read-heavy workloads with MySQL 8.x and PostgreSQL 16+.
Eloquent in Laravel 13 handles backed enums more gracefully, including nullable enums and enum arrays, with the AsEnumCollection cast storing an array of enum values in a JSON column.
Laravel 13 removes the app/Http/Kernel.php file; all middleware configuration lives in bootstrap/app.php.
New Artisan commands in Laravel 13 include make:dto, analyse, and route:conflicts.
Laravel 13 drops support for PHP 8.2 and 8.3, requiring PHP 8.4+ minimum.
Deprecated methods removed in Laravel 13 include Route::controller(), $request->has() with array syntax, Model::unguard(), and Str::slug() with custom separator as second positional arg.
Job payloads in Laravel 13 use a more compact serialization format, causing jobs queued by Laravel 12 to fail on a Laravel 13 worker.
Default pagination in Laravel 13 returns 25 items per page instead of 15.
Laravel 13 was released in Q1 2026.

sources.title: Laravel 13 Breaking Changes: The Real List | Marco Orta
claims: Laravel 12 stopped receiving bug fixes on August 13, 2026.
Laravel 13 requires PHP 8.3 minimum and supports up to PHP 8.5.
The CSRF middleware VerifyCsrfToken is renamed to PreventRequestForgery in Laravel 13 and adds origin verification.
The default cache configuration in Laravel 13 includes `serializable_classes => false`.
Laravel 13 validates that `uniqueBy` is not empty for `upsert` operations with MySQL or MariaDB.
Default cache prefixes in Laravel 13 change from underscore to hyphen.
The `JobAttempted` event in Laravel 13 exposes the exception object instead of a boolean.
The `$connection` property in `QueueBusy` is renamed to `$connectionName` in Laravel 13.
Container::call in Laravel 13 respects nullable defaults.
Routes with an explicit domain are evaluated before routes without one in Laravel 13.
